method_note: Read the full paper including the converted supplementary files (MOESM1 item list, MOESM2 patient-cohort sheet). Cohort of 6 CCDD patients; only patients 1 and 2 (GAMT deficiency) are in scope; patients 3-6 (CRTR/SLC6A8) get no rows and are counted in cohort_size_as_stated. Labels follow the bare-number 'Patient' column of Table 1 ('Table 1 #1', 'Table 1 #2'); the supplement uses the same numbering. The supplement row 'Segregation studies: Parents heterozygous carriers' describes tested parents for both patients, so each patient has two parent rows ('parent of Table 1 #n', 'parent of Table 1 #n 2'; sex not stated), with a heterozygous carrier variant row each. A short Python script assembled the JSON from my reading and sliced spans from the table rows; every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Choices and contradictions: (1) Consanguinity contradiction for patient 1: the Results text says both GAMT patients are 'of consanguineous descent' but the supplement family-history row gives 'Consanguinity: unknown' for patient 1; recorded 'not reported' for patient 1 (patient 2 'yes' in both). (2) Inheritance of the homozygous variants recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because both parents are stated carriers and the enum has no biparental option. (3) Variant type for patient 1: authors write 'homozygous duplication', recorded 'other' (not derived from the HGVS fs); patient 2 'homozygous splice error (intronic substitution)' recorded 'splice'. Literature column: patient 1 variant 'reported', patient 2 'novel'. (4) Table 1 prints the patient 2 variant with thin spaces ('c.391 + 5G > C'); the supplement prints 'c.391+5G>C'. (5) 'Movement disorders: no', 'Autism spectrum disorder/ challenging behaviour: no' and 'Cerebral magnet resonance abnormalities: no' (patient 2) were recorded as excluded features in the paper's words, but not used to exclude narrower checklist items (dystonia, ataxia, chorea, tremor, autistic features, aggressive behaviour, MRI items), which stay 'not reported'. Patient 1 MRI abnormalities 'yes' are unspecified, so MRI checklist items stay 'not reported'. (6) Elevated urinary guanidinoacetate comes from a sentence naming 'the two GAMT deficiency patients' (evidence basis 'inferred from group statement'); the individual values come from the supplement laboratory row. Plasma GAA and MRS creatine values were not turned into features because no reference range or abnormality statement is given per patient. Vital status not stated. Age values in Table 1 use the column units (months for first symptoms, years for ages), quoted as second spans.
